GMZ005-192130
Synopsis for Keys coastal waters from Ocean Reef to Dry Tortugas 424 AM EST Thu Nov 19 2026

SYNOPSIS

An expansive high pressure system over the Mid-Atlantic states will meander in place for the next few days. It will begin to slowly weaken heading into the weekend as it slowly drifts eastward out into the North Atlantic. In addition, a developing area of low pressure off the East Coast of Florida will move northward. Breezes will continue to slacken this morning as the main weather system move away. However, as the low strengthens, it may tighten the gradient just enough for Friday through Saturday to result in another brief wind surge, especially off the Upper Keys. Winds will also clock around to the west to northwest. As we head into early next week, the Keys will remain in overall weak flow with mainly light to potentially gentle breezes.

The Approximate Shoreward Edge of the Gulf Stream as of November 16, 2026...

32 NM south of Dry Tortugas Light, on Loggerhead Key 36 NM south of Cosgrove Shoal Light, off the Marquesas Keys 39 NM south of Sand Key Light, off Key West 37 NM south of Looe Key, off Big Pine Key 25 NM southeast of Sombrero Key Light, off Marathon 30 NM south of Alligator Reef Light, off Islamorada 15 NM southeast of Molasses Reef Light, off Key Largo 7 NM east of Carysfort Reef Light, off Ocean Reef

Gulf Stream Information Courtesy of the National Weather Service in Key West, using data from RTOFS and NASA SPoRT sea surface temperatures.
